To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are elevated levels of potential hazardous elements in the top soil of the central part Prague and their bioavailability needs to be studied.
there are elevated levels of potential harmful elements, such as As, Ba, Cd and Zn in the central part of city of Prague and their bioavailability and potential health risk should be studied.
The topsoil of Prague city centre is contaminated with a number of potentially harmful elements, and that their concentrations are significantly influenced by traffic and burning of fossil fuel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of element concentrations in the topsoils of Prague parks.
the identification of the main geochemical trends in topsoil of Prague, the identification of the most important elements and the assessment of their potential hazard.
the geochemical background, the geochemical mapping of urban soils and their comparison to agricultural soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the geochemistry of the soil in the central part of this city is influenced by a number of factors, and the results of the URGE project are an important part of the geochemical database for this area.
the city of Prague is not contaminated with hazardous elements.
the city of Prague topsoil has a higher potential of harmful elements than grazing land soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
geochemical mapping of urban soils is a valuable tool for assessing the level of potential harmful element contamination in urban environments.

there is a need for further studies of soil pollution by potentially toxic trace elements in the top of soil in the urban environment, and for the development and implementation of remediation technologies.

the results of the study are comparable with the results of other studies in European cities and that they can be used for the evaluation of the potential harmfulness of elements to humans and the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the geochemical mapping of soil can be a useful tool for the identification of potential hazardous trace elements contamination of urban soil, and for the assessment of the impact of different sources on the level of contamination.
the URGE project is very useful for the comparison of urban geochemistry of different European cities.
the URGE project is a good example of the benefits of a standardised sampling, preparation and analysis methodology for geochemical studies.
